title: ‎د ذ ر ز: letters that do not connect

blocks.text: With ⁧د ذ ر ز⁩ complete the six letters that do not link to the next ( ⁧ا و د ذ ر ز⁩ ) and learn two new sounds for Italian: the ⁧ذ⁩ the sound of dental interdental ⁧ز⁩ , which is not the Italian z. Finally you read broken words in more strokes without hesitation.

rows: 5–6 hours · one week at a standard pace

blocks.text: Materials This unit, calligraphy L0-03, Anki deck (tag L0-03)
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. recognize, pronounce and write ⁧د ذ ر ز⁩ in their two forms;
2. read and write words composed of several separate traits;
3. distinguish by ear d/ ḏ / z e ṯ / ḏ;
4. to pronounce the Arabic word at one beat;
5. read, write and translate the words of the vocabulary, including ⁧دِين⁩ "Religion" and ⁧دَيْن⁩ The amount of the debt shall be the amount of the debt.
Plan of the week.
7 Correction · Anki · review

The letters ⁧ا و د ذ ر ز⁩ they stick to the previous but never to the next. After each of them, the word starts again with a new trait: for this reason some words seem to be broken into two or three pieces even though they are one word.
⁧زَيْتُون⁩ zaytūn 3 ⁧ز⁩ · ⁧يتو⁩ · ⁧ن⁩
Reading, do not be fooled by the interior spaces: the space between two words is wider than that between two traits of the same word. Writing, keep the inner gaps tight.
1.1 Two families of forms
• ⁧د⁩ and ⁧ذ⁩ They are small and angular and rest on the line.
• ⁧ر⁩ and ⁧ز⁩ are curves and descend below the line.
The above point distinguishes ⁧ذ⁩ from ⁧د⁩ and ⁧ز⁩ from ⁧ر⁩ . If you confuse ⁧ذ⁩ and ⁧ز⁩ , look where the stroke ends: on line ( ⁧ذ⁩ ) or below ( ⁧ز⁩ ).
1.2 Sound and deafness
Arabic opposes deaf consonants (without vibration of vocal cords) and sound (with vibration) at the same point as the mouth. You already know some of them:
alveoli, African ⁧س⁩ s (L0-06) ⁧ز⁩ z
Put two fingers on your throat: with ⁧ذ⁩ and ⁧ز⁩ feel the vibration, with ⁧ث⁩ No.
• Sound. /d/, occlusive sound dental: tip of the tongue against the back of the upper incisors, such as d Italian di .
• Tracked. A short oblique stretch from top to bottom, then the horizontal base to the left on the line.
It doesn't go under the line.
• Examples ⁧دَار⁩ dār · ⁧دِين⁩ dīn · ⁧بَارِد⁩ bārid (final, isolated after ⁧ر⁩ ).
• Typical error. Connect it to the next letter.
• Sound. /ð/, fricativa interdentale sonora: the same position as ⁧ث⁩ , with the tongue between the teeth, but with the ropes vowels vibrating. It's the sound of English "this" .
• Tracked. How ⁧د⁩ , with one point above.
• Examples ⁧ذَنْب⁩ ḏanb Blame it.
• Typical error. Pronouncing it d o z. Test: pronunciation ⁧ث⁩ long, then add the voice without moving language.
• Note on dialects. In Egypt and the Levant ⁧ذ⁩ becomes d or z ( ⁧ذَهَب⁩ "gold" → dahab). In MSA it remains /ð/.
• Sound. /r/cellular. She's normally at a heartbeat by herself [ɾ], such as r of "caro" (caro), double (with šadda, L0-04)
It is vibrated [r], as in the cart. Close to a and u is often somewhat dark, and the neighboring vowel slightly lags back.
• Tracked. A curve that starts at the height of the line and descends below it to the left.
• Examples ⁧نُور⁩ nūr · ⁧بَرِيد⁩ barīd (final after ⁧ب⁩ ).
• Typical error. Put it on the line so that it can be confused with ⁧د⁩ .
• Sound. /z/, sound alveolar fricativa: is the s of "wrong" or "stop" , not the z of "unzio" or "zero" , The Z Italian is a cold [ts] or [dz]; the Arabic one has no initial t or d.
• Tracked. How ⁧ر⁩ , with one point above.
• Examples ⁧زَيْت⁩ zayt · ⁧وَزِير⁩ wazīr · ⁧تَزْوِير⁩ tazwīr.
• Typical error. Pronouncing .
2.5 Minimum pairs
⁧وَزِير⁩ ★ wazīr Minister ⁧و ز ر⁩ name m. · pl. ⁧وُزَرَاء⁩ wuzarāʾ

Notes of use. ⁧دَار⁩ dār: Female without ⁧ة⁩ · ⁧دَيْن⁩ dayn: Couple with ⁧دِين⁩ dīn · ⁧نَار⁩ nār: Female without ⁧ة⁩ · ⁧دَوْر⁩ dawr: ⁧لَعِبَ دَوْرًا⁩ It has played a role. ⁧بَرِيد⁩ barīd: ⁧البَرِيد الإِلِكْتْرُونِيّ⁩ E-mail: ⁧تَزْوِير⁩ tazwīr: ⁧تَزْوِيرُ الوَثَائِقِ⁩ • forgery of documents • forgery of documents. Two female without ⁧ة⁩ : ⁧دَار⁩ and ⁧نَار⁩ . In Arabic, gender is not always seen by form; We'll signal it in the vocabulary.
3.1 The words in context

Without vowels, ⁧دين⁩ read dīn "Religion" or "dayn" is debited. In an economic article ⁧الدين العام⁩ It is almost certainly the public debt () in an article on society ⁧الدين⁩ is the religion. This is the first case where the choice between two readings completely changes the sense of a sentence: accustomed to declaring on which clue context you base.

Oral production
1. From ⁧ث⁩ a ⁧ذ⁩ . Pronunciation ṯṯṯ with your hand on your throat, then add the voice: ḏḏḏ. Alternate ten times, then read ⁧ذَنْب⁩ .
2. ⁧ز⁩ Without t. Say a long s, add the entry: zzz. Then zayt, wazīr, tazwīr Without any "ts"
3. A heartbeat. Read nūr, barīd, bārid with a short r, as in "caro" (caro).
4. Registration. Record timed reading; check ḏ Interdental, z without t, diphthongs of dayn and zayt.
